question: If I use Relentless Pursuit on a unit at Vilemaw's Lair, can I move that unit to the other battlefield?
answer:
Yes, you can move a unit from Vilemaw's Lair to another battlefield using Relentless Pursuit.

The restriction on Vilemaw's Lair specifically states: "Units can't move from here to base." It does not prevent units from moving between battlefields (often referred to as "Ganking" when done via a Standard Move, or simply moving via a spell effect).

Key Details:

- Destination Matters: Vilemaw's Lair only blocks the "Base" as a valid destination for a move. Since you are moving the unit to the "other battlefield," the restriction does not apply.
- Relentless Pursuit Effect: The spell allows you to move a friendly unit. As long as the destination is not your base, the move resolves normally.
- Conquer Trigger: Note that Relentless Pursuit grants the unit an ability: "When I conquer, you may move me to my base." If the unit moves to the other battlefield and conquers it, that specific triggered move will fail because Vilemaw's Lair's restriction (preventing moves to base) would still apply if the unit is still at the Lair (though in this scenario, the unit has already moved to the other battlefield, so it would be able to move to base from that new location).

Related Ruling:
According to official FAQ guidance regarding Vilemaw's Lair: *"Vilemaw's Lair only prevents moving from Vilemaw to base. It... does not prevent moving from Vilemaw to another battlefield."

question: Does Ava Achiever trigger Teemo Strategist when you play a card with the Hidden keyword from your hand?
answer:
Ruling: Teemo Strategist will never trigger from Ava Achiever. Ava Achiever lets you play a card that has the Hidden keyword from your hand, but does not let you hide a card.

Nuances:

- This interaction was the same both before and after the Teemo Strategist errata

question: Will Rebuke spell return unit, including attached equipments to owner's hand?
answer:
No, the attached equipment will not return to your hand.

According to RiftJudge FAQ #8967 and Rule 422.4.b, when a unit is returned to your hand (such as by the effect of Rebuke), any gear attached to that unit does not return to your hand with it. Instead, the gear detaches and remains at the battlefield where the unit was previously located.

Following the resolution of the spell, because the gear is now an un-attached card present at a battlefield, it will be Recalled to your base during the next cleanup phase (per Rule 452.1).

question: Does Defiant Dance need to target 2 units? Can they target the same unit?
answer:
Yes, Defiant Dance must target two different units.

According to the card's text, it instructs you to give a unit +2 [S] and "another unit" -2 [S]. As confirmed by RiftJudge FAQ #2956, the word "another" indicates that the two targets must be distinct; therefore, you cannot target the same unit twice, nor can you play the spell if there is not a second valid unit available to target.

Additionally, per RiftJudge FAQ #2002, you must be able to select two distinct valid targets to play the spell.

question: If you have Dame the Despoiler at a battlefield and the opponent attacks in with a unit that has deflect, can you choose not to pay the deflect cost to avoid having to use her on defend ability?
answer:
You don't need to — you can simply target Dame herself instead of the attacking Deflect unit.

Dame's triggered ability says "choose a unit here" — it does not force you to choose the attacker. Since abilities can target their own source (Rule 355.9.c), you can choose Dame herself. Deflect only applies to spells and abilities an opponent controls that choose the Deflect unit (Rule 809.1.c), so targeting your own Dame costs nothing extra. The ability still resolves: her Might becomes her own Might (no change), and she gets +1 Shield.

If instead you wanted to avoid the ability entirely — you can't, because it's a mandatory trigger (no "may"). But you always have Dame as a free, legal target, so the Deflect cost never comes up unless you volunteer to point the ability at the attacker.

question: Rek'Sai Breacher, "Friendly Units played from anywhere other than a player's hand have ACCELERATE." Does this mean, if I play a card from deck it gets played ready? Or do I have to pay 1 power and 1 energy for it to be ready?
answer:
When you play a unit from your deck (or anywhere other than your hand) while you control Rek'Sai, Breacher, that unit gains the Accelerate keyword.

Accelerate does not automatically make the unit enter ready. Instead, it grants you the option to pay an additional cost to have it enter ready.

According to Rule 805.1.a and RiftJudge FAQ #9271:

- Accelerate is functionally short for: "As you play me, you may pay [1] Energy and 1 Power as an additional cost. If you do, I enter ready."
- If you do not pay this cost, the unit will enter the battlefield exhausted (the default state for units).
- If you do pay the cost, the unit will enter the battlefield ready.

In summary: You must pay the 1 Energy and 1 Power cost if you want the unit to enter ready. If you choose not to pay, it enters exhausted.

question: Does Sneaky Deckhand score a point when played directly to an empty battlefield?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, if you play Sneaky Deckhand directly into an empty battlefield you will conquer it, score a point, and be in control of it.

Nuances:

- The card bypasses the movement requirement, but movement is not required to conquer a battlefield
- Playing directly to a battlefield still counts as conquering if the battlefield is empty

question: If I use Ride the Wind to move a unit to an empty battlefield I own on my opponent's turn, do I get a conquer point?
answer:
Ruling: Yes, you get a conquer point when you use Ride the Wind to move a unit to an empty battlefield you own on your opponent's turn.

Sequence:

- You control both battlefields
- Opponent trades on battlefield A (making it empty)
- Opponent attacks battlefield B
- You use Ride the Wind to move your unit to the now-empty battlefield A
- You gain a conquer point

question: If I am holding Grove of the Garden with Blue Sentinel, do I draw 2 cards extra?
answer:
Yes, you draw 2 cards total — that's 1 extra card beyond the normal 1.

When you hold the battlefield where Blue Sentinel is at Grove of the God-Willow, Blue Sentinel's passive causes all your hold effects at that battlefield to trigger an additional time. Grove's "When you hold here, draw 1" triggers normally once, then a second time, for a total of 2 draws. You do not draw 3 cards (the extra trigger gives +1 additional draw, not +2).

Blue Sentinel also makes its own "When I hold, Add [A]" trigger twice, giving you 2 Power at the start of your next Main Phase.

question: Can I play Shen as a reaction at a battlefield when my opponent moves their unit there to conquer, if I don't have a unit at that battlefield? If yes, would Shen be an attacker or defender?
answer:
Ruling: You cannot play a unit at a battlefield unless you are in control of that battlefield. Since you have no unit at the battlefield, you cannot play Shen there as a reaction.

Nuances:

- This rule applies even when reacting to an opponent's conquest attempt
